A black hole between about 100 and 100,000 Suns. Few have been found.
A black hole gives off no light, so astronomers look for what it does to everything around it.
A black hole is a ball so small that the escape speed is more than the speed of light, about 300,000 km per second. Nothing can travel faster than light, so nothing that is inside can get out.
A black hole is a hole
A black hole is described by very few numbers: its mass, how fast it spins and its electric charge. Everything else about what fell in is lost to the outside.
A black hole is not a hole in space. It is a lot of mass squeezed into a very small volume, so squeezed that its gravity becomes extreme close to it.
A black hole of millions to billions of Suns, found in the centre of most large galaxies.
A cloud of gas and dust in space, where stars may be born or where a dying star has thrown off its layers.

A star shines because fusion in its core pushes outward while gravity pulls inward. When a very massive star (roughly 20 or more times the Sun) runs out of fuel, its core collapses in a fraction of a second.

Andromeda is a spiral galaxy in the constellation Andromeda. It is larger than the Milky Way and has more stars, though the Milky Way may hold more dark matter. It is the farthest thing most people can see with the naked eye.

Andromeda is moving toward us at about 110 km per second. The two galaxies will most likely begin to merge in roughly 4 to 5 billion years, and settle into one big elliptical galaxy that people sometimes call Milkomeda.

Apollo 15 was the first mission with a Moon buggy, and explored the foot of the Apennine mountains.
Apollo 16 explored the Descartes highlands by rover and brought back about 95 kg of rocks.

At about −235 °C, Triton is one of the coldest places anyone has measured in the solar system.
At the centre sits Sagittarius A*, a black hole of 4.3 million Suns. Dust hides the centre in visible light, so astronomers use infrared and radio telescopes to look through it.

At the centre, Einstein’s theory of gravity (general relativity) says all the mass is squeezed into a single point of infinite density. Most physicists read that as a sign that the theory breaks down there. A full theory of quantum gravity is needed, and we do not have one yet. Nobody knows what is really at the centre.
Before 1924 many astronomers thought the Milky Way was the whole universe. Edwin Hubble then measured the distance to Andromeda and showed it was a separate galaxy, far outside ours.
Bend the sky, size any black hole and slow down a clock. It all runs in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.
Between the two lie intermediate black holes, roughly 100 to 100,000 Suns. They are hard to find. One strong sign was a merger seen in 2019 that left a black hole of about 140 Suns.
Black holes are cosmic vacuum cleaners

Black holes do not suck things in from far away. If the Sun were swapped for a black hole of the same mass, Earth would keep orbiting exactly as it does now, only in the dark and the cold. Gravity far away depends on mass, not on what the mass is made of.

Blue light comes from hot young stars, so blue galaxies are still making stars. Red galaxies have mostly old stars and have stopped. This is why spirals look blue-white in the arms and ellipticals look yellow-red.
Callisto is far enough from Jupiter to get less of its harsh radiation, so scientists have suggested it for a future base.
Callisto is one of the most heavily cratered places in the solar system, and its surface is very old.

Cassiopeia is a W or an M, depending on the hour and the season, made of five fairly bright stars. It lies on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper, so when one is low the other is high. In the old story she was a queen who boasted of her beauty.
Chang'e 4 made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon, inside the huge South Pole-Aitken basin, in January 2019.
Chang'e 5 brought back about 1.7 kg of Moon samples in December 2020, the first new samples in 44 years.
China's Chang'e 3 put the Yutu rover on the Moon in December 2013, the first soft landing there since 1976.
China's Zhurong landed in May 2021, making China the second country to drive a rover on Mars.
City lights wash out faint galaxies. Move away from them and avoid the Moon.
Cosmic rays with far more energy than any collider have hit Earth for billions of years, and nothing has happened.

Count me as an active user: the app sends a random number made on your phone, at most once every few hours, with no username. It is not linked to you or your account. It is kept for 90 days and is used only to show how many people use Astryl.

Crux, the Southern Cross, is the smallest of all the constellations but one of the most famous. Four bright stars make a cross, and the two stars of its long arm point towards the south celestial pole, so it helps travellers find south. It cannot be seen from most of the northern half of the world.
Curiosity landed in Gale crater in August 2012 and showed that the place could once have supported microbial life.

Cygnus the Swan flies along the Milky Way. Its brightest stars form the Northern Cross, with Deneb at the top, the tail of the swan. Away from city lights the Milky Way looks like a pale river of light running through the swan, and binoculars show that it is made of countless faint stars. Summer and autumn evenings are the best time.

Galaxies range from dwarfs with a few thousand stars to giants with trillions. The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across. A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion km.
Galaxies were not born big. They grew, mostly by merging.

Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system. It is even bigger than Mercury.
Ganymede is the only moon known to have a magnetic field of its own.
Gas collapses into the first giant stars, which light up the dark universe.

Gas that spirals in forms an accretion disk. Friction heats it to millions of degrees, so it glows brightly in X-rays. Around the biggest black holes this glow makes a quasar, which can outshine a whole galaxy.

Gemini the Twins are marked by two bright stars, Castor and Pollux, standing side by side like the heads of two brothers. Pollux is the brighter one and has an orange tint. Castor is really a system of six stars. Look for them high in the sky on winter and spring evenings in the north.
Going from the Sun to the whole observable universe is a jump of about 600 quadrillion times (6 × 10¹⁷). Light, the fastest thing there is, needs 4.6 seconds to cross the Sun.

Gravity bends light so strongly that, at 1.5 times the horizon radius, light can travel in a circle around the black hole. This is why pictures from the Event Horizon Telescope show a bright ring around a dark centre. The dark “shadow” is about 2.6 times wider than the horizon itself.
Gravity bends light, so a black hole can act like a lens and distort or magnify what is behind it. This gravitational lensing also helps find hidden masses.

Gravity bends light, so a black hole in front of stars acts like a lens. Drag the black hole across the sky and watch the stars behind it stretch into arcs and a bright ring, called the Einstein ring. Use the slider to make it heavier.
Gravity pulls harder on the part of you that is closer. Falling feet first, your feet are pulled harder than your head, and you are stretched. Scientists call it spaghettification.

In 1974 Stephen Hawking showed that quantum effects make a black hole give off a very faint heat. The bigger the black hole, the colder it is. A black hole with the mass of the Sun would be about 60 billionths of a degree above absolute zero, colder than the 2.7 degrees of space itself, so today it takes in more than it gives out.

Leo the Lion is one of the few constellations that really looks like its animal. A backward question mark of stars, the Sickle, forms the head and chest and ends at bright Regulus, the lion’s heart. The triangle of stars to the east is its hindquarters. Spring evenings are the best time in the north.

Lyra the Lyre is small but holds Vega, one of the brightest stars of the northern sky. Vega is blue-white and, together with Deneb in Cygnus and Altair in Aquila, forms the Summer Triangle. Right next to Vega, a small parallelogram of stars makes the body of the lyre.

Most large galaxies have a black hole in the middle with millions or even billions of Suns. How they grew so big so early in the universe is still being studied. They probably started as smaller seeds, swallowed gas, and merged with other black holes.
Most large galaxies have a supermassive one at the centre.
Most of the Milky Way’s mass is not stars. The total of about 1.5 trillion Suns is mostly dark matter, which we know only from how it pulls on stars and gas.

Near a black hole of about 10 Suns the stretching is deadly well before the horizon. Near a supermassive black hole like Sagittarius A* the horizon is so large that the stretching there is gentle: you could cross it without feeling anything special, and be torn apart only later, deeper inside.

Polaris, the North Star, sits at the tip of the Little Bear’s tail. It hardly moves because it lies almost exactly above Earth’s north pole, so the whole sky seems to turn around it.
